title: Configure/disable light/dark mode custom variables?
impact: 3 reactions; most people asking to disable the toggles are hitting #821. kizu's follow-up asks for configurable variable names and omitting the setup, which the maintainer declined for names in #708 (interop between separately compiled files).
summary: The --lightningcss-light/dark toggles are emitted next to color-scheme only when light-dark() lowering is active. They can already be disabled with `exclude: Features.LightDark` (documented in transpilation.md's feature flag list) or by targets that support light-dark() natively (Chrome/Edge 123, Firefox 120, Safari 17.5). Configurable names were declined in #708.
repro: 828-repro.mjs (controls only): `:root{color-scheme:light dark}.a{color:light-dark(#fff,#000)}` with chrome 90 + exclude LightDark -> unchanged, no toggles; safari 17.5 -> no toggles; safari 17.4 -> polyfilled.
evidence: repro.mjs: all controls correct on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1. Compat boundary matches @mdn/browser-compat-data css.types.color.light-dark (chrome 123, firefox 120, safari 17.5).

subcases.case: kizu: custom variable names / omit setup

draftReply:
This can be turned off with the `LightDark` feature flag: pass `exclude: Features.LightDark` to `transform()` (or Vite's `css.lightningcss.exclude`), and Lightning CSS keeps `light-dark()` as written and no longer adds the `--lightningcss-light`/`--lightningcss-dark` variables. Raising your targets to browsers with native support (Chrome 123, Firefox 120, Safari 17.5) has the same effect. The flags are listed at https://lightningcss.dev/transpilation.html#feature-flags.

If you're turning it off because colors don't follow a nested `color-scheme`, that's tracked in #821. Custom variable names were discussed in #708: the shared names let separately compiled stylesheets work together.

Closing since this is supported, but feel free to reopen if the flag doesn't cover your case.
